content: Cefdinir should only be prescribed when there is a confirmed or strongly suspected bacterial infection or a clear prophylactic indication. Prescribing it in the absence of these conditions is unlikely to benefit the patient and increases the risk of developing drug-resistant bacteria. Prolonged use of broad-spectrum antibiotics like cefdinir may lead to the emergence and overgrowth of resistant organisms. Patients undergoing treatment should be closely monitored, and if a superinfection occurs, an appropriate alternative therapy should be initiated. Caution is advised when prescribing cefdinir to individuals with a history of colitis. In patients with transient or persistent renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance <30 mL/min), the total daily dose of cefdinir should be reduced. This is because standard doses can lead to high and prolonged plasma concentrations of the drug. Patients should be informed that cefdinir and other antibacterial drugs are only effective against bacterial infections and should not be used to treat viral infections, such as the common cold. When prescribed cefdinir, patients should be advised to complete the full course of therapy as directed, even if they feel better early in the treatment. Skipping doses or not completing the therapy may reduce the effectiveness of the treatment and increase the likelihood of bacterial resistance, making future infections harder to treat. Antacids containing magnesium or aluminum interfere with cefdinir absorption. If such antacids are needed, cefdinir should be taken at least two hours before or after the antacid. Similarly, iron supplements, including multivitamins containing iron, also interfere with cefdinir absorption. If iron supplements are required, cefdinir should be taken at least two hours before or after the supplement. Foods highly fortified with iron, such as certain breakfast cereals, have not been studied for their effects on cefdinir absorption. Diarrhea is a common side effect of antibiotics, including cefdinir, and usually resolves after discontinuation of the antibiotic. However, patients may develop watery and bloody stools, with or without stomach cramps and fever, even up to two months after completing the antibiotic course. If this occurs, patients should contact their physician immediately. Concomitant administration of cefdinir with antacids containing aluminum or magnesium reduces the rate and extent of cefdinir absorption by approximately 40%, and the time to reach peak plasma concentration is prolonged by one hour. To avoid this interaction, cefdinir should be taken at least two hours before or after the antacid. Probenecid inhibits the renal excretion of cefdinir, leading to approximately double the area under the curve (AUC), a 54% increase in peak plasma levels, and a 50% prolongation in the apparent elimination half-life of cefdinir. When cefdinir is taken with therapeutic iron supplements containing 60 mg of elemental iron or multivitamins supplemented with 10 mg of elemental iron, the extent of cefdinir absorption is reduced by 80% and 31%, respectively. If iron supplements are necessary, cefdinir should be taken at least two hours before or after the supplement. There have been reports of reddish stools in patients taking cefdinir, often in conjunction with iron-containing products. This discoloration is due to the formation of a nonabsorbable complex between cefdinir or its breakdown products and iron in the gastrointestinal tract. Cefdinir may cause false-positive reactions for ketones in urine tests using nitroprusside but not with tests using nitroferricyanide. It may also result in false-positive reactions for glucose in urine when using Clinitest®, Benedict’s solution, or Fehling’s solution. Enzymatic glucose oxidase-based tests, such as Clinistix® or Tes-Tape®, are recommended. Cephalosporins, including cefdinir, may occasionally induce a positive direct Coombs’ test. The carcinogenic potential of cefdinir has not been evaluated. It showed no mutagenic effects in the bacterial reverse mutation assay (Ames test) or the point mutation assay at the hypoxanthine-guanine phosphoribosyltransferase locus in V79 Chinese hamster lung cells. No clastogenic effects were observed in vitro in the structural chromosome aberration assay in V79 Chinese hamster lung cells or in vivo in the mouse bone marrow micronucleus assay. In rats, fertility and reproductive performance were not affected by cefdinir at oral doses up to 1000 mg/kg/day (70 times the human dose based on mg/kg/day, 11 times based on mg/m²/day). Maternal toxicity, such as decreased body weight gain, was observed in rabbits at the maximum tolerated dose of 10 mg/kg/day without adverse effects on offspring. Decreased body weight occurred in rat fetuses at doses ≥100 mg/kg/day and in rat offspring at doses ≥32 mg/kg/day. No effects were observed on maternal reproductive parameters or offspring survival, development, behavior, or reproductive function. However, there are no adequate and well-controlled studies in pregnant women. Cefdinir should only be used during pregnancy if clearly needed, as animal reproduction studies are not always predictive of human response. Cefdinir has not been studied for use during labor and delivery. Following a single 600 mg dose, cefdinir was not detected in human breast milk. The safety and efficacy of cefdinir in neonates and infants less than six months of age have not been established. Its use for treating acute maxillary sinusitis in pediatric patients (ages six months to 12 years) is supported by evidence from studies in adults and adolescents, the similar pathophysiology of acute sinusitis in adults and children, and comparative pharmacokinetic data in the pediatric population. The efficacy of cefdinir in geriatric patients is comparable to that in younger adults. Clinical trials have shown that cefdinir is well-tolerated across all age groups, with geriatric patients experiencing a lower rate of adverse events, including diarrhea, compared to younger adults. Dose adjustment in elderly patients is not necessary unless renal function is significantly impaired.
